title: Matplotlib Grid Lines
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and main concepts of Matplotlib Grid Lines.
Create a Matplotlib Figure and Axes suitable for the visualization task.
Apply the relevant plotting API and configure its key properties.
Inspect plotted artists or chart properties to verify the intended result.
Choose labels and visual encodings that communicate data accurately.
prerequisites: NumPy arrays and basic numeric data

understand.concept: Grid lines provide visual guides aligned with axis ticks. Matplotlib can show grids on both axes or only one axis, and their style, color, width and transparency can be configured. Grid lines should support reading values without overpowering the data.
understand.whyItMatters: A restrained grid can make comparisons easier, especially when values need to be read against a scale.
understand.analogy: Grid lines are like faint ruled lines on graph paper that help estimate positions.
understand.summary: Matplotlib Grid Lines is part of the Matplotlib learning path. The examples use deterministic data and the Agg backend for automated execution.

explain.narrative: Read the concept, execute each example in sequence, inspect the printed result and compare it with the expected output. Each example creates a figure with the non-interactive Agg backend and closes it after inspection.

examples.title: Enable grid lines
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.grid(True)
print(ax.get_xgridlines()[0].get_visible())
plt.close(fig)

examples.title: Show only horizontal grid lines
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.grid(True, axis='y')
print(ax.get_ygridlines()[0].get_visible())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: The axis argument limits grid lines to y.

examples.title: Choose a dashed grid style
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.grid(True, linestyle='--')
print(ax.get_xgridlines()[0].get_linestyle())
plt.close(fig)

examples.title: Set grid transparency
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.grid(True, alpha=0.4)
print(ax.get_xgridlines()[0].get_alpha())
plt.close(fig)
examples.explanation: A lower alpha makes grid lines less prominent.

examples.title: Disable the grid
examples.code:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.grid(False)
print(ax.get_xgridlines()[0].get_visible())
plt.close(fig)
